output.question: Find the top trending Python and Rust repos this week and this month, rank by momentum, and keep only what's relevant to agentic / MCP / dev-tooling with a one-line why-it-matters each.
output.findings:
The current landscape is dominated by agentic tooling, specifically focused on coding assistants, agent governance, and specialized skill sets for LLMs. Key Python projects include 'microsoft/markitdown' for data ingestion, 'anthropics/claude-code' for terminal-based agentic workflows, and 'microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit' for security and reliability. These tools are critical for building production-ready, secure, and efficient AI agents.

In the Rust ecosystem, momentum is concentrated on high-performance infrastructure for agents. 'farion1231/cc-switch' provides a unified interface for various coding agents, 'screenpipe/screenpipe' offers local, privacy-focused activity recording for AI, and 'run-llama/liteparse' delivers high-speed document parsing. These projects highlight a shift toward Rust for performance-critical agent components.

'chopratejas/headroom' stands out as a cross-language utility (Python/MCP) for token optimization, demonstrating the growing importance of cost-efficiency in agentic pipelines. Similarly, 'mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills' and 'awslabs/aidlc-workflows' represent the trend toward standardizing agent capabilities and operational lifecycles, essential for enterprise-grade agent deployment.
